title: Code Reviewer dispatch webhook, version 1
description: The signed wake-up call of the Webhook-Trigger (#316, #318): after a job is enqueued the app sends POST <dispatch URL> to the Dispatcher, which then claims exactly that job (claim by job id is the idempotency point; a replay finds a job that is not due and gets 204). The body is DispatchWebhook: closed, at most 1 KiB, no secret and no repository data. Headers: Content-Type: application/json; X-Dispatch-Timestamp (Unix seconds, decimal); X-Dispatch-Id (the dispatchId of the body); X-Dispatch-Key-Id (which signing key, to rotate with a current and a previous key); X-Dispatch-Signature: 'v1=' followed by the lower case hexadecimal HMAC-SHA-256, keyed with the secret of that key id (UTF-8 text), over the UTF-8 text 'v1:{timestamp}:{dispatchId}:{rawBody}' where rawBody is the request body exactly as sent. The signing secret is distinct from every other secret. A receiver checks, in this order: content type and size; the headers' form (malformed); the timestamp within the tolerance of its own clock, 300 seconds either way (expired); the key id against its current and previous key (unknown_key); the signature in constant time (bad_signature); only then parses the body against DispatchWebhook (closed schema) and requires its dispatchId to equal the header. The verdicts and a vector for each are in dispatch-signing-vectors.json (DispatchSigningVectors). A receiver answers at once: 202 DispatchAccepted, 200 DispatchIgnored, 429 or 503 with Retry-After, and 401/400/413 with the runner API's ErrorResponse for what it refuses, the same for every kind of refusal. THE STOP CALL (#487): when a job's claim ends the app sends POST <dispatch URL with its last path segment replaced by 'stop'> with the closed body DispatchStop (type 'job.stop', jobId, stopId, sentAt). It is signed and verified exactly like the wake-up call (same headers, same signing rule, same order of checks, same current and previous key, same 300 second window, same 1 KiB limit and same refusals), with one difference: X-Dispatch-Id carries the stopId and must equal the body's stopId. The receiver stops only the VMs it created for that job (tagged with the app and the job id) and does nothing else; no VM means 200. A stopId it has handled is answered 200 and does nothing (replay protection); a stop that failed on the platform's side is not remembered, so the same call can be repeated. Answers: 202 DispatchStopAccepted (VMs are being stopped), 200 DispatchStopIgnored (nothing to stop, or a replay), 503 with Retry-After when the platform could not be asked, and 401/400/413 as for the wake-up call. A receiver of an earlier release has no such route and answers 404: the sender logs it and goes on, the reaper cleans up. Both ends read this file: the app (app/integration-tests/compatibility), the runner (runner/tests/contract) and the Dispatcher project check its examples.

DispatchWebhook.description: The body of the wake-up call. Closed: an unknown field, such as a secret, a token, a credential, a signature or repository data, is refused. A sender never adds one and a receiver refuses a body that has one.

attempt.description: The number of the attempt the job is on (1 for the first).

dispatchId.description: The id of this call, new for every send of the same job (a UUID).

KnownDispatchIgnoredReason.description: Why a receiver answered 200 ignored. `not_claimable`: the claim of that job answered 204 (not due, running, finished, cancelled, superseded, or the pool cap is reached); the app resends after its acknowledgement timeout. `not_capable`: the receiver cannot run that review kind; the app stops resending that kind. A reader accepts any reason of the right form.

DispatchAccepted.description: 202 from the receiver: the wake-up call is verified and the claim goes on in the background.

DispatchIgnored.description: 200 from the receiver: verified, and there is nothing to start.

DispatchStop.description: The body of the stop call (#487). Closed, at most 1 KiB, no secret and no repository data. `stopId` is new for every stop of a job and is also the X-Dispatch-Id header; a receiver remembers the ones it handled, so a replay does nothing. The same signing rule as the wake-up call, over this body.

stopId.description: The id of this stop (a UUID), equal to the X-Dispatch-Id header.

DispatchStopAccepted.description: 202 from the receiver: the stop call is verified and the VMs of the job are being stopped in the background. `vms` (#493, optional) names them, so that the app can take the moment of this answer as the end of each VM's billable minutes; a receiver of the earlier release leaves it out, and the sender then falls back to the bounded estimate (contracts/README.md, "Rolling out the billable minutes").

DispatchStopIgnored.description: 200 from the receiver: verified, and there is nothing to do. `no_vm`: the job has no VM (it never had one, or it is stopped already). `replayed`: this stopId was handled before.

DispatchSigningVectors.description: The file dispatch-signing-vectors.json: signing keys of the example (dummy values), the tolerance, and requests as a receiver sees them with the verdict each must get. A consumer (the app's sender and the Dispatcher's receiver, in TypeScript, and the runner suite in Python) computes the verdict itself and compares. Header names are lower case.

body.description: The raw body exactly as received.

DispatchSigningKey.description: A signing key of the example. The secret is a dummy; a real one is at least 32 characters and unique to this purpose.
